title: Four Thousand Weeks
author: Oliver Burkeman
blurb: Oliver Burkeman, a former productivity enthusiast, argues that most time management advice rests on an impossible promise: that with enough efficiency, we can finally get on top of everything. The average human life lasts only about four thousand weeks, and no system can make that enough for all our ambitions. Worse, becoming more efficient often just brings more demands. Drawing on philosophy and psychology, Burkeman suggests a different path: accept your limits, make hard choices about what to neglect, and stop treating the present as a mere stepping stone to some future moment of control. He explores why we flee into distraction, why patience is a superpower, why rest needs no justification, and why time is richer when shared with others. The result is a liberating, deeply humane guide to spending a finite life well.

lessons.t: You Only Get Four Thousand Weeks
lessons.b: An average life lasts about four thousand weeks, and facing that limit honestly is the starting point for using time well.
